committee: CC City Council Meeting of the Whole
overview: The Medford City Council Committee of the Whole serves as a legislative and evaluative body comprising all council members to review municipal operations, policy ordinances, annual budgets, and community development plans. The committee has met consistently across recorded sessions spanning from August 2022 through October 2026. Key areas of recurring work include annual operating budget reviews, comprehensive zoning ordinance updates, Community Preservation Act recommendations, CDBG annual action plans, and municipal tree regulations. In its October 2026 meeting, the committee voted to enter executive session to discuss strategy regarding pending litigation.

threads.name: Annual budget preparation and fiscal planning
threads.summary: Across consecutive fiscal years, the committee evaluates municipal operating budgets, revenue estimates, fixed cost projections, and departmental funding requests prior to full council action. Early in the 2022–2023 term, the committee reviewed municipal finances and conducted departmental reviews for the FY24 budget. In subsequent terms, the body established formal processes to aggregate collective council budget priorities before holding preliminary budget hearings for FY25, FY26, and FY27. At its May 2026 preliminary hearings, the body reviewed departmental requests across executive, elections, fire, and library budgets before referring revised figures and questions to the administration.

threads.name: Comprehensive zoning ordinance updates
threads.summary: The committee works to align Medford's zoning code with comprehensive plans, housing targets, and state mandates. Early efforts focused on recodification cleanup, scoping Phase Two revisions, and developing consultant RFPs for multi-family overlay districts under the MBTA Communities Act. Through 2024 and 2025, the committee monitored zoning updates across corridors such as Mystic Avenue and Salem Street alongside consultant Innes Associates. In late 2026, the committee reviewed draft recommendations for affordable housing linkage fees and advanced a new consultant RFP for the next phase of the Zoning Updates Project.

threads.name: Community Preservation Act project funding
threads.summary: The committee annually evaluates project funding requests recommended by the Community Preservation Committee for open space, historic preservation, and affordable housing. In early 2023, the committee favorably referred 11 initial project recommendations totaling various historic, recreational, and housing initiatives. Similar annual reviews followed in early 2024 and 2025, recommending approvals for park upgrades, cemetery maintenance, and trust allocations. In January 2026, the body favorably referred an 11-project package totaling approximately $2.4 million across field lighting, ADA access, historic restorations, and housing assistance.

threads.name: Community Development Block Grant action plans
threads.summary: The committee conducts annual reviews of the city's Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Action Plans, receiving requests from municipal offices and non-profit service providers. In April 2023, the body reviewed public service applications for Year 49 CDBG funds before placing the overview on file for a public hearing. Subsequent annual reviews in 2024 and 2025 evaluated federal allocations for housing stabilization, food security, elder transportation, and youth services. In April 2026, the committee reviewed the Program Year 52 CDBG Action Plan proposing $1.433 million in federal funds before referring it for a final vote.

threads.name: Tree preservation and canopy regulation
threads.summary: The committee has repeatedly considered ordinances regulating public trees, private tree removal during development, and the establishment of a municipal Tree Committee. Initial discussions in late 2022 and early 2023 focused on aligning public tree definitions with state forestry laws and modeling private tree protection on zoning mitigation. In late 2024, the committee referred public and private tree drafts to working groups and department heads to assess operational authority and simplify regulatory language. In mid-2025, the committee approved and referred an amended Tree Committee ordinance to the City Council, followed by referring an amended Public Tree Ordinance out of committee in July 2026.

threads.name: Regulation of food trucks and mobile vendors
threads.summary: The committee has worked to establish a formal licensing and permitting framework for stationary food trucks operating during single-day and special events. In late 2022 and early 2023, members voted to narrow draft regulations to event-specific licenses while protecting brick-and-mortar businesses. In November 2023, the committee considered restructuring the rules to delegate food safety oversight to the Board of Health while retaining city control over public ways. In March 2024, the paper was kept in committee to allow legal redrafting to clarify jurisdictional boundaries over municipal property and streamline administrative permits.

threads.name: Solid waste and curbside collection contracts
threads.summary: The committee addressed municipal waste collection, recycling, and composting infrastructure to replace expiring service contracts and control rising costs. In early 2023, members reviewed a draft waste removal request for proposals evaluating curbside composting and collection frequencies. In August 2023, the committee reviewed a 10-year solid waste contract incorporating weekly food waste composting and preferred commercial hauler programs. In September 2023, the committee approved amendments to update the solid waste ordinance and referred it for departmental and legal review.

threads.name: City charter revision and municipal governance
threads.summary: The committee evaluates charter amendments to modify legislative authority, executive appointments, and representation structures. In April and May 2023, the body reviewed targeted charter amendments regarding council budget authority, independent council staffing, and confirmation of board appointments. In 2024, the committee incorporated charter review into its term governing agenda and monitored mayorally submitted draft revisions. In March 2025, the committee voted to recommend a council composition model consisting of five at-large seats and four district seats before referring the draft charter to the full council.
